question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the radical as a fractional exponent:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{9}}{\sqrt[3]{{y}^{7}}}=\frac{{y}^{9}}{{({y}^{7})}^{1/3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we apply the power rule for exponents:

$$
\frac{{y}^{9}}{{({y}^{7})}^{1/3}}=\frac{{y}^{9}}{{y}^{7(1/3)}}=\frac{{y}^{9}}{{y}^{7/3}}
$$

Then, we apply the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{9}}{{y}^{7/3}} & = \\ {y}^{9-7/3} & = \\ {y}^{20/3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we express the result as a radical:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{20/3} & =\sqrt[3]{{y}^{20}}\end{aligned}
$$
